questions.q: Which of the following best defines accounting as a discipline?
o: The process of preparing government budgets alone
The process of calculating company taxes only
The process of recording, classifying, summarizing and interpreting financial transactions
The process of only recording cash transactions in a diary
questions.e: Accounting is the systematic process of recording, classifying, summarizing and interpreting financial data so that users can make informed decisions. The other options describe only a small part of this process, not the whole discipline.
questions.p: Accounting na the process wey dem dey record, classify, summarize and interpret financial transactions well-well. The other options na just small part of am, dem no cover everything.

questions.q: Which of these is classified as an INTERNAL user of accounting information?
questions.e: Internal users are people inside the organisation, such as management, who use accounting information daily for planning and control. Tax authorities, creditors and investors are outside the business, so they are external users.
questions.p: Internal users na people wey dey inside the business, like management, wey dey use the information every day for planning and control. Tax people, creditors and investors dey outside the business, so na external users dem be.

questions.q: A bank manager wants to decide whether to grant a loan to Chidinma's Bakery in Enugu. Which accounting information will be most useful to the bank manager?
o: The names of the bakery's suppliers
The statement of financial position showing assets and liabilities
The minutes of the last staff meeting
The advertising jingles used by the bakery
questions.e: A lender needs to know the business's financial strength before giving a loan, and the statement of financial position shows assets, liabilities and net worth. Staff meeting minutes, jingles and supplier names do not reveal financial soundness.
questions.p: Person wey wan give loan need know how strong the business be for money matter, and na the statement of financial position go show the assets, liabilities and net worth. Staff meeting gist, jingle and supplier names no fit show financial strength.

questions.q: Which branch of accounting is mainly concerned with ascertaining the cost of producing goods and services in order to help management control expenses?
questions.e: Cost accounting focuses on calculating and controlling the cost of production so that management can set prices and reduce waste. Financial accounting reports overall results, auditing checks accuracy, and public sector accounting deals with government funds.
questions.p: Cost accounting dey focus on how to calculate and control production cost so management fit set price and reduce waste. Financial accounting na for general report, auditing na to check am, public sector accounting na for government money.

questions.q: Bookkeeping is different from accounting mainly because bookkeeping:
o: involves only the recording of day-to-day business transactions
involves interpreting financial statements for decision making
involves preparing tax returns for government
questions.e: Bookkeeping is simply the clerical task of recording daily transactions in the books of account, while accounting goes further to classify, summarize and interpret the data for decision making. Tax preparation and auditing are separate specialised activities, not bookkeeping itself.
questions.p: Bookkeeping na just the work of recording daily transactions for book, but accounting pass am because e dey classify, summarize and interpret the data make people fit decide well. Tax preparation and auditing na different work entirely, no be bookkeeping.

questions.q: Trade union leaders representing workers at Zenith Textiles Plc want to negotiate for better wages. Which accounting information would be most relevant to support their case?
o: The personal bank statements of the managing director
The company's logo and marketing slogan
The list of raw materials suppliers
The company's profit and loss account showing the level of profit made
questions.e: Employees and their unions use the profit and loss account to see how profitable the company is, which helps them argue for a fair share through better wages. The director's personal account, the logo and the supplier list have nothing to do with wage justification.
questions.p: Workers and dem union go use the profit and loss account to see how the company dey make money, so dem fit argue say make dem get better pay. The director personal account, logo and supplier list no get anything to do with wage matter.

questions.q: One of the following is NOT a significance (importance) of accounting to a business organisation. Which one?
o: It helps in ascertaining profit or loss
It helps in planning and decision making
It helps in controlling the weather for farming activities
It helps in assessing the financial position of the business
questions.e: Accounting deals with financial records and decision-making, not with natural events like weather, which is outside its scope. The other three options are genuine benefits that accounting provides to a business.
questions.p: Accounting na about money matter and decision, e no be about weather wey be natural thing wey accounting no fit control. The other three options na real benefits wey accounting dey give business.

questions.q: Why are external auditors considered important users of accounting information in a company?
o: They need the records to supervise the daily production process
They need the records to verify that the financial statements give a true and fair view
They need the records to fix the selling prices of goods
They need the records to recruit new staff for the company
questions.e: External auditors examine a company's accounting records and statements independently to confirm that they present a true and fair view, which protects shareholders and other stakeholders. Setting prices, supervising production and recruiting staff are management duties, not the auditor's role.
questions.p: External auditors dey check company books independently to confirm say the financial statements show true and fair view, and dis one dey protect shareholders and other people wey get interest. To set price, supervise production or recruit staff na management work, no be auditor work.

questions.q: Which accounting concept states that a business is treated as a unit separate and distinct from its owner(s), so that the owner's personal transactions are not mixed with the business records?
questions.e: The business entity concept says the business is a separate accounting unit from the owner. This is why an owner's personal spending, like school fees, is not recorded in the business books.
questions.p: Business entity concept dey talk say business na separate thing from di owner. Na why owner personal spending, like school fees, no go enter business book.

questions.q: Alhaja Fatima's company is expected to continue operating for the foreseeable future, so its assets are recorded at cost rather than at the price they would fetch if the business were to be closed down immediately. Which accounting concept is being applied?
questions.e: The going concern concept assumes the business will continue to operate indefinitely, so assets are valued at cost of use, not forced sale/liquidation value.
questions.p: Going concern concept dey assume say business go still dey operate for future, so dem go value assets based on cost, no be say business wan close now-now.

questions.q: A company has used the straight-line method of depreciation for its delivery vans for the past five years. Which accounting concept requires that the company should NOT switch to the reducing balance method without good reason, and must disclose any such change?
questions.e: The consistency concept requires that once an accounting method is adopted, it should be applied from one period to another so that financial statements can be compared over time. Changes must be justified and disclosed.
questions.p: Consistency concept say once company choose one method, dem must dey use am every year so dat people fit compare di accounts well-well. If dem wan change am, dem must give good reason and talk am open.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa has 100 bags of rice in his store at the end of the year. Each bag cost ₦5,000 to buy, but due to a fall in market price, each bag can now only be sold for ₦4,500 (net realizable value). Under the prudence concept, at what value should the closing stock of rice be reported in the financial statements?
questions.e: The prudence concept requires stock to be valued at the lower of cost and net realizable value. Since ₦4,500 (NRV) is lower than ₦5,000 (cost), stock = 100 x ₦4,500 = ₦450,000.
questions.p: Prudence concept say make dem use di lower price between cost and net realizable value for stock. Since ₦4,500 dey lower pass ₦5,000, dem go use am: 100 x ₦4,500 = ₦450,000.

questions.q: Mr. Okafor's accountant refused to record the 'excellent team spirit' of the company's staff as an asset in the statement of financial position of Okafor Ventures. This refusal is best explained by which accounting concept?
questions.e: The money measurement concept states that only items that can be expressed in monetary terms are recorded in the accounts. Team spirit, though valuable, cannot be reliably measured in naira, so it is excluded.
questions.p: Money measurement concept say na only tins wey you fit put money value go enter di account. Team spirit, even though e good, you no fit put naira figure on top am, so e no go enter book.

questions.q: Chika Stores paid ₦180,000 as rent covering the period 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2024 (12 equal months). If the company's financial year ends on 31 December 2023, how much rent expense should be charged to the 2023 financial statements under the matching (accrual) concept?
questions.e: Only the rent relating to the 2023 period (October, November, December = 3 months) should be charged to 2023, the rest is a prepayment for 2024. Monthly rent = ₦180,000/12 = ₦15,000, so 3 months = ₦45,000.
questions.p: Na only di rent wey belong to 2023 (Oct, Nov, Dec = 3 months) go enter 2023 account, di rest na prepayment for 2024. One month rent = ₦180,000/12 = ₦15,000, so 3 months = ₦45,000.

questions.q: Adaeze Enterprises bought a small stapler for ₦1,500, expected to last for 5 years. Instead of recording it as a non-current asset and spreading its cost through depreciation, the accountant charged the full ₦1,500 as an expense in the year it was bought. Which accounting concept justifies this treatment?
questions.e: The materiality concept allows items of very small (insignificant) value to be treated in the simplest way, such as charging them off as an expense immediately, since treating them as an asset would not meaningfully affect the financial statements.
questions.p: Materiality concept allow small small amount wey no go really affect di account to dey treated simple way, like to just charge am as expense one time, instead of to dey spread am as asset for years.

questions.q: A business has total assets of ₦800,000 and total liabilities of ₦350,000. Applying the dual aspect (accounting equation) concept, what is the value of the owner's capital (equity)?
questions.e: The dual aspect concept is expressed as Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Rearranging, Capital = Assets - Liabilities = ₦800,000 - ₦350,000 = ₦450,000.
questions.p: Dual aspect concept na Assets = Liabilities + Capital. If you rearrange am, Capital = Assets - Liabilities = ₦800,000 - ₦350,000 = ₦450,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'source document' in accounting?
o: A document issued only by commercial banks to their customers
A summary document prepared after the final accounts have been drawn up
A document used only to prepare the trial balance
A document that provides evidence of a business transaction and contains details used to record it in the books
questions.e: A source document is the original evidence of a transaction (e.g. invoice, receipt, cheque) from which entries are first made in the books of original entry. It is prepared at the time the transaction happens, not after final accounts.
questions.p: Source document na the first paper wey show say transaction happen, e dey contain all the details wey dem go use enter am for book. E no be summary wey dem do after final accounts.

questions.q: Which source document is prepared by a seller and sent to a buyer when goods are sold on credit?
questions.e: An invoice is the document a seller issues to a buyer showing details of goods sold on credit, including quantity, price and amount owed. A receipt is for cash already paid, while credit and debit notes are for adjustments after the sale.
questions.p: Invoice na the paper wey the seller give the buyer wen e sell goods on credit, e dey show quantity, price and the amount wey the buyer owe. Receipt na for when money don already pay, while credit and debit note na for correction after sale.

questions.q: Chidinma bought goods worth ₦40,000 on credit from Mama Nkechi's store. Three days later, she returned damaged goods worth ₦5,000 to the store. Which source document will Mama Nkechi issue to Chidinma to acknowledge the returned goods?
questions.e: When a seller receives returned goods from a customer, the seller issues a credit note to reduce the amount the customer owes. A debit note would instead be issued by the buyer or to increase a customer's debt.
questions.p: Wen seller receive goods wey customer return, dem go give am credit note to reduce the money wey e owe. Debit note na different thing, na to increase wetin customer owe or wen buyer dey send am.

questions.q: Baba Sule's business was undercharged by ₦2,000 on an invoice for goods it bought on credit from a supplier. Which document will the supplier send to Baba Sule to correct this undercharge?
questions.e: A debit note is issued when a seller wants to increase the amount a buyer owes, such as correcting an undercharge on a previous invoice. A credit note does the opposite, reducing the amount owed.
questions.p: Debit note na wetin seller go send wen e wan increase wetin buyer owe, like wen dem undercharge am for invoice before. Credit note na im dey do the opposite, e dey reduce the debt.

questions.q: All credit purchases of goods meant for resale are first recorded, from the source documents, in which book of original entry before being posted to the ledger?
questions.e: The purchases journal (also called purchases day book) is used to record all credit purchases of goods meant for resale, based on invoices received from suppliers. Cash purchases go to the cash book instead.
questions.p: Purchases journal na where dem dey first write all credit purchases of goods wey dem wan resale, based on invoice wey supplier give. Cash purchases na im dey enter cash book.

questions.q: When a trading business returns goods earlier bought on credit back to its supplier, in which book of original entry will this transaction first be recorded?
questions.e: Goods returned to a supplier are called returns outwards (or purchases returns) from the buyer's point of view, and are recorded in the returns outwards journal using the debit note received. Returns inwards journal is for goods customers return to the business.
questions.p: Wen business return goods wey e buy on credit back to supplier, na returns outwards (purchases returns) dem dey call am, and dem go record am for returns outwards journal based on debit note. Returns inwards na for wen customer return goods come back to the business.

questions.q: On the same day, Alhaji Musa's shop sold goods on credit worth ₦45,000 to Tunde, and also received a cheque of ₦30,000 from Ngozi in settlement of an old debt. In which books of original entry will these two transactions, respectively, first be recorded?
questions.e: The credit sale to Tunde is first entered in the sales journal because it is a credit sale of goods. The cheque received from Ngozi is a cash/bank receipt, so it goes straight into the cash book, not the sales journal again.
questions.p: The credit sale wey dem give Tunde na im dem go first enter inside sales journal because na credit sale of goods. The cheque wey come from Ngozi na cash/bank money wey enter, so na cash book e go enter, no be sales journal again.

questions.q: Which of the following transactions would normally be recorded in the journal proper (general journal) rather than in any special book of original entry?
o: Purchase of a delivery van on credit for business use
Credit sale of goods to a customer
Credit purchase of goods meant for resale
questions.e: The journal proper records transactions that do not fit the special books, such as the credit purchase of a fixed (non-current) asset like a delivery van, since it is not goods for resale. Credit sales, credit purchases of trading goods, and cash transactions each have their own special books.
questions.p: Journal proper na where dem dey record transactions wey no fit enter the special books, like wen business buy delivery van on credit, because the van no be goods for resale. Credit sales, credit purchase of trading goods and cash transactions get their own special books.

questions.q: The double entry principle in accounting states that every business transaction has a dual effect. Which of the following best describes this principle?
o: One account is affected, either debited or credited
Two accounts are affected, one debited and the other credited
Three accounts are affected, all debited
Two accounts are affected, both credited
questions.e: Double entry means every transaction affects at least two accounts: one account is debited while another is credited by the same amount. This keeps the accounting equation balanced.
questions.p: Double entry mean say every transaction dey touch at least two accounts: dem go debit one, dem go credit another one with the same amount. Na so the accounting equation go still balance.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly states one of the basic rules of double entry for a personal account?
o: Debit all expenses, credit all assets
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
Debit what goes out, credit what comes in
Debit all liabilities, credit all expenses
questions.e: For personal accounts, the rule is 'debit the receiver, credit the giver', because the person receiving value owes the business, while the one giving value is being paid or credited.
questions.p: For personal account, the rule be say make you debit the person wey receive, credit the person wey give. Na because the receiver dey owe the business, while the giver dey get credit.

questions.q: Adaeze Stores bought office equipment worth ₦150,000 and paid immediately by cheque. Which two accounts are affected and how should the entries be made?
o: Debit Cash account; Credit Office Equipment account
Debit Bank account; Credit Office Equipment account
Debit Office Equipment account; Credit Cash account
Debit Office Equipment account; Credit Bank account
questions.e: Office equipment (an asset) is coming into the business, so it is debited. Payment is by cheque, so the Bank account (an asset going out) is credited.
questions.p: Office equipment na asset wey dey enter business, so dem go debit am. Dem pay with cheque, so e mean money dey comot from Bank, so Bank account go dey credit.

questions.q: The Furniture account of Bello Ventures for the month of March showed the following: Debit side - Balance b/d ₦45,000, Purchase of furniture on credit ₦25,000. Credit side - Furniture sold for cash ₦10,000. What is the balance carried down (c/d) on the Furniture account at the end of the month?
questions.e: Total debit entries = 45,000 + 25,000 = 70,000. Subtract the credit entry of 10,000 (furniture sold) to get the balance c/d: 70,000 - 10,000 = ₦60,000.
questions.p: Total wey dem debit na 45,000 + 25,000 = 70,000. Comot the 10,000 wey dem credit (furniture wey dem sell), you go remain with 70,000 - 10,000 = ₦60,000.

questions.q: In the classification of ledger accounts, the Rent Expense account is best described as a ___ account.
questions.e: Nominal accounts deal with expenses, losses, income, and gains. Rent paid is an expense, so Rent Expense account is a nominal account.
questions.p: Nominal account na for expenses, losses, income and gains. Rent wey dem pay na expense, so Rent Expense account na nominal account.

questions.q: A sole trader, Mr. Yakubu, withdraws ₦20,000 cash from the business for his personal use. Which account should be debited to record this transaction?
questions.e: When an owner takes money for personal use, the Drawings account is debited to show a reduction in the owner's investment, while the Cash account is credited since cash is going out.
questions.p: When owner carry money comot for personal use, dem go debit Drawings account to show say the owner don reduce im capital, while Cash account go dey credit because cash don comot.

questions.q: Chinedu's Cash account for the month of June showed the following: Debit side - Balance b/d ₦120,000, Cash sales ₦85,000. Credit side - Purchases ₦60,000, Rent paid ₦15,000, Wages ₦20,000. What is the balance c/d (closing balance) on the Cash account?
What best describes a cash book in financial accounting?
o: A book of original entry that records both cash and bank transactions as they occur
A ledger account used only for recording fixed assets
A statement that shows the profit or loss for a trading period
A record that shows only credit sales and credit purchases
questions.e: The cash book is a book of original entry (and also serves as a ledger account) that records all cash and bank receipts and payments in the order they happen. It is not used for fixed assets, profit/loss, or credit transactions alone.
questions.p: Cash book na book wey dem dey use record all cash and bank transactions as e dey happen. E no be for fixed assets, profit/loss, or only credit transactions.

questions.q: In a three-column cash book, what are the discount columns used for?
o: Recording only the discount received from suppliers each month
Recording cash discount allowed to debtors and cash discount received from creditors
Recording bad debts written off at the end of the year
Recording trade discount allowed on bulk purchases of goods
questions.e: The discount columns in a three-column cash book are memorandum columns that record cash discount allowed (to customers who pay promptly) and cash discount received (from suppliers when we pay promptly). Trade discount and bad debts are not recorded here.
questions.p: Di discount columns for three-column cash book na to show discount wey we give customers (discount allowed) and discount wey suppliers give us (discount received) when payment dey done quick. Trade discount and bad debt no dey enter dia.

questions.q: Chidinma's cash column in her cash book showed an opening balance of ₦5,000. During the week she received ₦12,000 cash from a customer and paid ₦3,500 cash for stationery. What is the closing cash balance?
questions.e: Closing cash balance = Opening balance + Receipts - Payments = 5,000 + 12,000 - 3,500 = ₦13,500.
questions.p: Closing cash balance = Opening balance + wetin enter - wetin comot = 5,000 + 12,000 - 3,500 = ₦13,500.

questions.q: A contra entry in a three-column cash book arises in which of the following situations?
o: When goods are sold on credit to a customer
When the discount allowed for the period exceeds the discount received
When a cheque received earlier from a customer is dishonoured by the bank
When cash is withdrawn from the bank for office use, affecting both the cash and bank columns
questions.e: A contra entry occurs when a transaction affects both the cash column and the bank column of the same cash book, such as withdrawing cash from the bank for office use (debit cash, credit bank). Credit sales, discount comparisons, and dishonoured cheques do not create contra entries by themselves.
questions.p: Contra entry dey happen when one transaction touch both cash and bank columns for same cash book, like when person comot money from bank go use for office (debit cash, credit bank). Credit sales or dishonoured cheque no be contra entry by demsef.

questions.q: Mr. Okafor owed a supplier ₦40,000. He paid the full debt by cheque within the discount period and enjoyed a 5% cash discount for prompt payment. How much did he actually pay?
questions.e: Discount = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Amount paid = ₦40,000 - ₦2,000 = ₦38,000. The debt reduces because of the discount received for paying promptly.
questions.p: Discount = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Wetin e pay = ₦40,000 - ₦2,000 = ₦38,000. Di debt reduce because e pay fast fast make im enjoy discount.

questions.q: A trader's three-column cash book showed opening bank balance of ₦25,000. During the month: (i) received a cheque of ₦18,000 from a debtor and banked it; (ii) paid rent by cheque, ₦6,000; (iii) withdrew ₦5,000 cash from the bank for office use (a contra entry); (iv) paid a supplier by cheque, ₦10,000. What is the closing bank balance?
questions.e: Closing bank balance = 25,000 + 18,000 (cheque received) - 6,000 (rent) - 5,000 (withdrawal to cash) - 10,000 (supplier) = ₦22,000. Discounts allowed or received do not affect the bank column figure directly.
questions.p: Closing bank balance = 25,000 + 18,000 (cheque wey enter) - 6,000 (rent) - 5,000 (wey e comot go cash) - 10,000 (supplier) = ₦22,000. Discount no dey change the bank column amount directly.

questions.q: A trader bought goods on credit worth ₦60,000 from Alhaji Musa. He later returned defective goods worth ₦5,000. He paid the balance owed in cash within the discount period and enjoyed a 2% cash discount on the amount paid. How much discount did he receive?
questions.e: Balance owed after returns = 60,000 - 5,000 = ₦55,000. Discount received = 2% of 55,000 = ₦1,100. The discount is calculated on the net balance, not the original purchase amount.
questions.p: Balance after return = 60,000 - 5,000 = ₦55,000. Discount wey e receive = 2% of 55,000 = ₦1,100. Na di balance wey remain dem use calculate discount, no be di original amount.

questions.q: Under the petty cash imprest system, the petty cashier is given a fixed sum of money at the start of each period, spends part of it on small office expenses, and is later given back exactly what was spent so that the fund returns to the same fixed amount. What is this system called?
questions.e: The imprest system is where a fixed float is given, spent, and then topped up by the exact amount spent, so the float always starts each new period at the same fixed level. This is the standard method for handling petty (small) cash.
questions.p: Imprest system na where dem give petty cashier fixed money, e go spend small-small for office, den dem go refund am the exact money wey e spend so the float go remain same level every time.

questions.q: In the operation of the petty cash imprest system, the amount given to the petty cashier by the head/main cashier at the end of a period to replace the exact total spent during that period, so as to restore the float to its fixed level, is called the?
questions.e: The reimbursement is the top-up money given back to the petty cashier equal to actual expenditure, restoring the float to the agreed fixed imprest amount. The imprest itself is the original fixed sum, while the float is the cash physically on hand at any time.
questions.p: Reimbursement na the money wey dem give back to petty cashier wey match the money e don spend, so the float go return to the fixed imprest amount. Imprest na the original fixed money, float na the cash wey dey hand at any time.

questions.q: Mama Chidinma operates the office petty cash book with a fixed imprest of ₦8,000. During the week she made the following payments: Postage ₦1,200; Stationery ₦950; Transport ₦1,800; Cleaning materials ₦550. How much must the head cashier give her at the end of the week to restore her imprest to ₦8,000?
questions.e: Total expenditure = 1,200 + 950 + 1,800 + 550 = ₦4,500. Under the imprest system, reimbursement always equals the total amount actually spent, not any other figure.
questions.p: Total money wey she spend = 1,200 + 950 + 1,800 + 550 = ₦4,500. Under imprest system, the reimbursement go always equal the total money wey dem spend.

questions.q: A petty cashier holds a fixed imprest of ₦10,000. During one week, he made the following payments: Transport ₦2,300; Postage ₦750; Entertainment ₦1,150; Sundry expenses ₦300. What is the balance in hand in the petty cash book before the head cashier reimburses him?
questions.e: Total spent = 2,300 + 750 + 1,150 + 300 = ₦4,500. Balance in hand = Imprest - Total spent = 10,000 - 4,500 = ₦5,500, which is the figure carried down before top-up.
questions.p: Total wey e spend = 2,300 + 750 + 1,150 + 300 = ₦4,500. Balance wey remain = 10,000 - 4,500 = ₦5,500, na im dem go carry down before dem reimburse am.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's office petty cash imprest is fixed at ₦12,000. At the start of a new month, before receiving any reimbursement, the petty cashier still had ₦1,500 left over from the previous month. How much must the head cashier give him so that his float returns to the full imprest of ₦12,000?
questions.e: The float must total ₦12,000. Since ₦1,500 is already in hand, the reimbursement needed is 12,000 - 1,500 = ₦10,500. Giving the full ₦12,000 again would wrongly double the float.
questions.p: Float suppose reach ₦12,000 total. Since ₦1,500 dey hand already, wetin dem go add na 12,000 - 1,500 = ₦10,500. If dem give the full 12,000 again, e go double the float wrongly.

questions.q: A company's petty cash imprest is fixed at ₦9,000. At the end of the month, the analysis columns of the petty cash book show the following totals: Postage ₦620; Stationery ₦980; Travelling ₦1,450; Cleaning ₦350; Sundry expenses ₦200. Assuming the petty cash book balances correctly, how much will the head cashier reimburse at the end of the month?
questions.e: Total expenditure = 620 + 980 + 1,450 + 350 + 200 = ₦3,600. Under the imprest system, the sum of the analysis columns must equal the total payments column, and this total is exactly what is reimbursed to restore the ₦9,000 imprest, regardless of the imprest figure itself.
questions.p: Total wey dem spend = 620 + 980 + 1,450 + 350 + 200 = ₦3,600. Under imprest system, the analysis columns total suppose match the total payment column, and na this total dem go reimburse make imprest return to ₦9,000.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a genuine advantage of operating the petty cash imprest system in a business office?
o: It limits the amount of cash that can be lost or misused at a time
It simplifies the control and checking of small routine payments
It reduces the workload on the main/head cashier
It allows large capital expenditures such as machinery purchases to be recorded through it
questions.e: The petty cash imprest system is designed only for small, routine, day-to-day office expenses like postage and stationery, not for large capital items such as machinery, which must pass through the main cash book or bank account. The other three options are real, well-known benefits of the system.
questions.p: Petty cash imprest system na for small small office spending like postage and stationery, e no be for big capital things like machine, wey suppose pass through main cash book or bank. The other three options na real correct advantages.

questions.q: In a petty cash book, the special columns used to classify and group each small payment under headings such as postage, stationery, travelling, and cleaning, in order to make posting to the ledger easier, are called?
questions.e: Analysis columns are the side-by-side columns in a petty cash book that break down each payment into its expense type, making it simple to total each type of expense and post it to the correct ledger account.
questions.p: Analysis columns na the columns for petty cash book wey dem dey use divide each payment according to the type of expense, e dey make am easy to total each expense type and post am go the correct ledger account.

questions.q: A bank reconciliation statement is best described as a statement that...
o: summarizes the profit or loss made by a business during a period
shows the total assets and liabilities of a business
reconciles the cash book balance with the bank statement balance by explaining the differences between them
records all cash transactions of a business during a period
questions.e: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to explain and agree the difference between the balance shown in the cash book and the balance shown on the bank statement. It does not record transactions, show assets/liabilities, or calculate profit.
questions.p: Bank reconciliation statement na di one wey dem dey use settle the gap between cash book balance and bank statement balance. E no be the one wey dem dey use record transactions, show property or calculate profit.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common reason why the balance shown in a firm's cash book may differ from the balance shown on its bank statement on the same date?
o: Cash sales recorded in the sales day book
Cheques issued to suppliers but not yet presented for payment by the beneficiary
Depreciation of fixed assets charged for the year
Purchase of stock on credit from suppliers
questions.e: Unpresented cheques are already deducted in the cash book but have not yet been paid out by the bank, so they cause a timing difference between the two balances. Sales day book entries, depreciation and credit purchases do not affect the bank balance directly.
questions.p: Cheque wey business don issue but di person wey go collect am never carry am go bank, dat one go cause the cash book and bank statement to no match for that moment. The other options no concern bank balance at all.

questions.q: Chidi's cash book showed a debit balance of ₦45,000 on 31 March. On comparing it with the bank statement, it was found that cheques of ₦12,000 issued to a supplier had not yet been presented for payment, while a cheque of ₦8,000 paid into the bank had not yet been credited by the bank. What is the balance shown on the bank statement?
questions.e: To move from the cash book balance to the bank statement balance, add back unpresented cheques (they are still in the bank's favour) and subtract uncredited lodgements (not yet added by the bank). So ₦45,000 + ₦12,000 - ₦8,000 = ₦49,000.
questions.p: To waka from cash book balance go bank statement balance, you go add the cheque wey dem never present and comot the money wey dem pay but bank never credit am. So ₦45,000 + ₦12,000 - ₦8,000 = ₦49,000.

questions.q: A firm's bank statement showed a credit balance of ₦60,000 as at 30 April. It was discovered that cheques amounting to ₦15,000 issued to suppliers had not yet been presented for payment, while a lodgement of ₦5,000 paid into the bank had not yet been credited by the bank. What is the balance as shown in the firm's cash book?
questions.e: To move from the bank statement balance to the cash book balance, subtract unpresented cheques and add uncredited lodgements. So ₦60,000 - ₦15,000 + ₦5,000 = ₦50,000.
questions.p: To waka from bank statement balance go cash book balance, comot the unpresented cheque and add the lodgement wey bank never credit. So ₦60,000 - ₦15,000 + ₦5,000 = ₦50,000.

questions.q: Adaeze's cash book showed a balance of ₦72,000 before reconciliation. On checking the bank statement, she discovered that the bank had charged ₦1,500 as commission and credited ₦2,500 as interest on her deposit account, neither of which had been entered in the cash book. What is the adjusted cash book balance?
questions.e: Items appearing only on the bank statement, such as bank charges and interest, must be entered in the cash book to update it. Subtract the charge and add the interest: ₦72,000 - ₦1,500 + ₦2,500 = ₦73,000.
questions.p: Anything wey dey only for bank statement like charge and interest, you go enter am for cash book to update am. Comot the charge, add the interest: ₦72,000 - ₦1,500 + ₦2,500 = ₦73,000.

questions.q: Okon's cash book showed a debit balance of ₦90,000 on 30 June. Further checks revealed that: (i) bank charges of ₦2,000 had not been entered in the cash book, (ii) a customer's cheque for ₦10,000, already recorded in the cash book, was dishonoured by the bank, (iii) cheques totalling ₦18,000 issued to suppliers had not yet been presented for payment, and (iv) a deposit of ₦6,000 had not yet been credited by the bank. What is the balance shown on the bank statement?
questions.e: First adjust the cash book for items known only from the bank statement: ₦90,000 - ₦2,000 (charges) - ₦10,000 (dishonoured cheque) = ₦78,000. Then reconcile to the bank statement by adding unpresented cheques and subtracting uncredited deposits: ₦78,000 + ₦18,000 - ₦6,000 = ₦90,000.
questions.p: First adjust the cash book with wetin bank statement show: ₦90,000 - ₦2,000 (charge) - ₦10,000 (dishonoured cheque) = ₦78,000. Then add the unpresented cheque and comot the deposit wey never enter bank: ₦78,000 + ₦18,000 - ₦6,000 = ₦90,000.

questions.q: A firm's bank statement showed a credit balance of ₦150,000 on 31 May. The following were discovered: cheques of ₦25,000 issued to suppliers had not yet been presented, a lodgement of ₦40,000 had not yet been credited by the bank, a standing order payment of ₦5,000 had not been entered in the cash book, and bank interest of ₦3,000 credited by the bank had also not been entered in the cash book. What was the cash book balance before these standing order and interest entries were made?
questions.e: First find the adjusted cash book balance using timing differences: ₦150,000 - ₦25,000 + ₦40,000 = ₦165,000. This adjusted figure already includes the standing order and interest, so the original balance before those entries is ₦165,000 - ₦3,000 (interest) + ₦5,000 (standing order) = ₦167,000.
questions.p: First find the adjusted cash book balance using the timing wahala: ₦150,000 - ₦25,000 + ₦40,000 = ₦165,000. Dis one don already carry the standing order and interest inside, so the original balance before dem enter am na ₦165,000 - ₦3,000 (interest) + ₦5,000 (standing order) = ₦167,000.

questions.q: A business prepares a bank reconciliation statement mainly in order to...
o: calculate the net profit of the business for the accounting period
determine the value of closing stock at the end of the trading period
compute the total amount of value added tax payable to government
detect errors and fraud and ensure the accuracy of both the cash book and bank records
questions.e: Bank reconciliation helps identify errors, omissions, or fraud by comparing the cash book with the bank statement, ensuring both records are accurate. It has nothing to do with calculating profit, valuing stock, or computing VAT.
questions.p: Bank reconciliation dey help catch mistake, omission or fraud by comparing cash book and bank statement, so both of dem go correct well well. E no concern profit calculation, stock value, or VAT computation.

questions.q: What is a trial balance in accounting?
o: A statement showing the list of debit and credit balances extracted from the ledger accounts to check the arithmetical accuracy of the books
A statement showing the profit or loss made by a business during a trading period
A book that records all cash transactions of a business
A statement showing the assets, liabilities and capital of a business as at a given date
questions.e: A trial balance simply lists all ledger balances (debit and credit) to check that total debits equal total credits. It is not the same as a profit and loss account or a statement of financial position.
questions.p: Trial balance na the list wey show all debit and credit balance from the ledger, to check sey the totals balance well-well. E no be the same thing as profit and loss or statement of financial position.

questions.q: Which of the following errors will NOT cause the trial balance to disagree?
o: A transaction completely omitted from both the debit and credit sides of the ledger
The debit entry of a transaction posted correctly but the credit entry omitted entirely
An error in adding up (casting) the figures in an account, affecting only one side
A balance carried down to the wrong side of an account
questions.e: If a transaction is left out completely from both sides, the debit and credit totals are both reduced equally, so the trial balance still balances. The other errors affect only one side of the double entry, so they cause a difference.
questions.p: If transaction no enter at all for both debit and credit side, the two totals go reduce equally, so e no go affect the balance. But the other ones touch only one side, so trial balance go disagree.

questions.q: Why is a suspense account opened in the ledger of a business?
o: To record discounts received from suppliers
To show the value of closing stock at year end
To record cash sales made during the period
To temporarily hold the difference between the debit and credit totals of a trial balance that fails to agree
questions.e: When a trial balance does not balance, a suspense account is opened to carry the difference temporarily until the errors causing the disagreement are found and corrected.
questions.p: If trial balance no balance, dem go open suspense account to hold the difference small time, until dem find the mistake wey cause am and correct am.

questions.q: A company bought a delivery van for ₦450,000 for use in the business, but the accountant debited the amount to the Purchases account instead of the Motor Vehicle (asset) account. What type of error is this?
questions.e: Purchases is an expense account while Motor Vehicle is a fixed asset account. Recording a transaction in the wrong class of account (expense instead of asset) is called an error of principle.
questions.p: Purchases na expense account but Motor Vehicle na asset account, two different class. Wen you use wrong class of account like this one, na error of principle dem dey call am.

questions.q: While extracting a trial balance, Miss Hauwa found that the total of the credit column exceeded the total of the debit column by ₦4,500. A suspense account was opened to make the trial balance balance. On which side of the suspense account was the ₦4,500 entered?
o: It is not entered in the suspense account
questions.e: Since the credit column is higher than the debit column, the suspense account must be given a debit balance of ₦4,500 so that when it is combined with the debit column, the two sides will agree.
questions.p: Since credit side pass debit side, dem go put the ₦4,500 for debit side of suspense account so that wen you add am, both sides go balance.

questions.q: A cheque of ₦2,500 received from a customer, Ngozi, was correctly entered in the Cash Book but was wrongly posted to the debit side of Ngozi's account in the sales ledger instead of the credit side. If this is the only error in the books, by how much will the trial balance disagree?
questions.e: Posting an amount to the wrong side of an account creates a double effect: the account is short by the amount it should have had on the correct side, plus it has an extra equal amount on the wrong side. So the error of ₦2,500 posted to the wrong side causes a gap of 2 x ₦2,500 = ₦5,000 between the debit and credit totals.
questions.p: Wen you post amount go wrong side of account, e dey cause double wahala: the correct side miss the amount, and the wrong side get extra amount. So ₦2,500 wey enter wrong side go cause gap of 2 x ₦2,500 = ₦5,000 between the debit and credit totals.

questions.q: In the preparation of final accounts for a sole trader, which account is prepared first to determine the gross profit or gross loss for the period?
o: Net profit or net loss account
questions.e: The trading account compares net sales with the cost of goods sold to arrive at gross profit or gross loss. This is prepared before the profit and loss account, which calculates net profit.
questions.p: Trading account na im dem dey use compare sales with cost of goods wey dem sell tosabi gross profit or loss. Na after dis one dem go prepare profit and loss account to find net profit.

questions.q: Which formula correctly calculates the cost of goods sold in a sole trader's trading account?
o: Opening stock plus Purchases minus Closing stock
Closing stock plus Purchases minus Opening stock
Opening stock minus Purchases plus Closing stock
Opening stock plus Closing stock minus Purchases
questions.e: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock. This represents the value of goods actually sold during the trading period.
questions.p: Cost of goods wey dem sell = Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock. Na so dem go sabi di value of goods wey don enter market for di period.

questions.q: Chidinma Enterprises recorded the following for the year: Sales ₦150,000; Opening stock ₦20,000; Purchases ₦90,000; Closing stock ₦15,000. What is the gross profit for the year?
questions.e: Cost of goods sold = 20,000 + 90,000 - 15,000 = ₦95,000. Gross profit = Sales - Cost of goods sold = 150,000 - 95,000 = ₦55,000.

questions.q: A sole trader's gross profit for the year was ₦55,000. During the same period, the following expenses were incurred: Rent ₦10,000; Salaries ₦15,000; Discount allowed ₦2,000. What is the net profit for the year?
questions.p: Net profit = Gross profit minus all expenses = 55,000 - (10,000 + 15,000 + 2,000) = 55,000 - 27,000 = ₦28,000.

questions.q: Mr. Obi, a sole trader, paid ₦24,000 as rent during the year. At the end of the accounting year, he discovered that ₦4,000 of this amount was paid in advance for the following year. What amount should be charged as rent expense in the profit and loss account for the current year?
questions.e: The ₦4,000 is a prepayment relating to next year, so it must be deducted from the amount paid. Rent expense for the year = 24,000 - 4,000 = ₦20,000, in line with the matching/accrual concept.
questions.p: Di ₦4,000 na prepayment wey belong to next year, so dem go comot am from di money wey e pay. Rent for dis year = 24,000 - 4,000 = ₦20,000, because of di matching concept.

questions.q: At the end of the financial year, a sole trader's total assets were valued at ₦250,000 while her total liabilities amounted to ₦80,000. What is the value of her capital at that date?
questions.e: Using the accounting equation, Capital = Total Assets - Total Liabilities = 250,000 - 80,000 = ₦170,000.
questions.p: With di accounting equation, Capital = Total Assets - Total Liabilities = 250,000 - 80,000 = ₦170,000.

questions.q: A sole trader bought equipment for ₦100,000 and depreciates it at 10% per annum using the straight line method. If the net profit before charging depreciation for the year was ₦60,000, what is the net profit after charging depreciation?
questions.e: Annual depreciation = 10% of ₦100,000 = ₦10,000. Net profit after depreciation = 60,000 - 10,000 = ₦50,000, since depreciation is an expense charged to the profit and loss account.
questions.p: Depreciation for di year = 10% of ₦100,000 = ₦10,000. Net profit after dem don remove depreciation = 60,000 - 10,000 = ₦50,000, because depreciation na expense wey dey enter profit and loss account.

questions.q: Which of the following final account statements shows the assets, liabilities and capital of a sole trader as at a particular date?
questions.e: The balance sheet, also called the statement of financial position, shows the assets, liabilities and capital of a business as at a specific date, unlike the trading and profit and loss accounts which cover a period.
questions.p: Balance sheet, wey dem still dey call statement of financial position, na im dey show assets, liabilities and capital of business for one particular date, unlike trading and profit and loss account wey dey cover period.

questions.q: An accrued expense in accounting is best described as:
o: Expense paid in advance before it is due
Income received before it is earned
Expense incurred during the accounting period but not yet paid
Income earned but not yet received
questions.e: An accrued expense is one that has been incurred (used/consumed) during the period but has not yet been paid for by year end, e.g. an unpaid electricity bill. It is shown as a current liability in the statement of financial position.
questions.p: Accrued expense na expense wey don happen (dem don use am) for this period but dem never pay for am before year end, like light bill wey never pay. Dem go show am as current liability.

questions.q: A prepaid expense in accounting is best described as:
o: Expense that has been written off as bad debt
Expense incurred but not yet paid
Payment made in the current period for a service to be enjoyed in a future period
questions.e: A prepaid expense is money paid in the current period for a benefit or service that will be enjoyed in a future accounting period, e.g. rent paid in advance. It is shown as a current asset.
questions.p: Prepaid expense na money wey dem pay now but the service or benefit go dey for future period, like rent wey dem pay before time. Dem go show am as current asset.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa paid ₦180,000 as rent during the year, and this amount covers 15 months from January of the current year to March of the following year. If his accounting year ends on 31 December, what amount should be charged as rent expense in the income statement for the year?
questions.e: Total rent paid (₦180,000) covers 15 months, so monthly rent = 180,000/15 = ₦12,000. Expense for the 12 months of the accounting year = 12,000 x 12 = ₦144,000. The remaining 3 months (₦36,000) is a prepayment carried to next year.
questions.p: Total rent wey dem pay na ₦180,000 for 15 months. One month rent na 180,000/15 = ₦12,000. For the 12 months wey concern dis year, expense na 12,000 x 12 = ₦144,000. The remaining 3 months (₦36,000) na prepayment.

questions.q: During the year, a trader paid electricity bills amounting to ₦260,000. At the end of the year, an additional bill of ₦35,000 relating to the current year had not yet been paid. What is the total electricity expense to be charged in the income statement for the year?
questions.e: Total electricity expense for the year = cash paid (₦260,000) plus the accrued bill not yet paid (₦35,000) = ₦295,000. The accrual concept matches expenses to the period they relate to, regardless of when cash is paid.
questions.p: Total electricity cost for the year na wetin dem pay (₦260,000) plus the bill wey never pay (₦35,000) = ₦295,000. Accounting rule talk say we go match expense to the period wey e belong, no matter if dem don pay am or not.

questions.q: Chidinma Traders wrote off ₦25,000 as bad debt during the year. Which of the following correctly states the effect of this transaction on the final accounts?
o: Decrease in net profit and decrease in debtors
Decrease in net profit and increase in debtors
Increase in net profit and decrease in debtors
Increase in net profit and increase in debtors
questions.e: Writing off bad debts is treated as an expense, so it reduces net profit. It also reduces the debtors (receivables) balance because the amount owed is no longer expected to be recovered.
questions.p: When dem write off bad debt, e dey reduce profit because na expense. E also dey reduce debtors balance because dem no go fit collect dat money again.

questions.q: At the end of the year, trade debtors amounted to ₦500,000. The business decided to maintain a provision for doubtful debts at 5% of debtors. The previous year's provision was ₦18,000. What amount will be charged to the income statement (profit and loss account) as provision for doubtful debts for the current year?
questions.e: New provision required = 5% x ₦500,000 = ₦25,000. Previous provision was ₦18,000. Since the new provision is higher, the increase of ₦25,000 - ₦18,000 = ₦7,000 is the amount charged as an additional expense in the income statement.
questions.p: New provision wey dem need na 5% x ₦500,000 = ₦25,000. Last year own na ₦18,000. Since new one pass old one, the increase of ₦25,000 - ₦18,000 = ₦7,000 na the amount wey dem go charge as expense this year.

questions.q: Trade debtors before adjustment stood at ₦620,000. During the year, further bad debts of ₦20,000 were discovered and must be written off. The business then wants to maintain a provision for doubtful debts at 4% of the remaining debtors. What is the net trade debtors figure to be reported in the statement of financial position after all adjustments?
questions.e: First remove the further bad debts: ₦620,000 - ₦20,000 = ₦600,000. New provision = 4% x ₦600,000 = ₦24,000. Net debtors in the statement of financial position = ₦600,000 - ₦24,000 = ₦576,000.
questions.p: First commot the new bad debt: ₦620,000 - ₦20,000 = ₦600,000. New provision na 4% x ₦600,000 = ₦24,000. Net debtors for balance sheet na ₦600,000 - ₦24,000 = ₦576,000.

questions.q: A prepaid expense at the end of the accounting year is shown in the statement of financial position as:
questions.e: A prepaid expense represents a benefit or service already paid for but not yet consumed, so it is a resource the business will benefit from in future - hence it is reported as a current asset.
questions.p: Prepaid expense na benefit wey dem don pay for but never use am finish, so na asset wey business go still enjoy later - na why dem dey show am as current asset.

questions.q: In accounting, depreciation of a non-current asset is best described as:
o: The cost of repairing and maintaining the asset
The systematic allocation of the cost of the asset over its useful life
The fall in the resale value of the asset in the open market
The amount set aside each year to buy a new asset
questions.e: Depreciation is an accounting process that spreads the cost of a non-current asset over the years it is used to earn income. It is not the same as a fall in market value, saving for replacement, or repair costs.
questions.p: Depreciation na how dem dey spread the cost of asset for the years wey the business go use am. E no be say the market price of the asset fall, and e no be money wey dem dey keep to buy new one or to repair am.

questions.q: Under the straight line method of depreciation, the annual depreciation charge is calculated as:
o: Net book value multiplied by a fixed percentage every year
Cost of asset divided by the number of years the asset has been used
(Cost of asset - Estimated residual value) divided by the estimated useful life
Market value of the asset minus its cost
questions.e: The straight line method charges an equal amount of depreciation each year, found by subtracting the residual (scrap) value from the cost and dividing by the useful life in years.
questions.p: Straight line method dey give equal depreciation every year. You go minus the scrap value from the cost, then divide the answer by the number of years wey the asset go dey used.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze bought a sewing machine for her tailoring shop in Onitsha for ₦450,000. It has an estimated useful life of 5 years and an estimated residual value of ₦50,000. Using the straight line method, what is the annual depreciation charge?
questions.e: Annual depreciation = (Cost - Residual value) / Useful life = (450,000 - 50,000) / 5 = 400,000 / 5 = ₦80,000.
questions.p: Annual depreciation = (Cost minus Residual value) divided by Useful life = (450,000 - 50,000) / 5 = 400,000 / 5 = ₦80,000.

questions.q: A grinding machine bought by Baba Yusuf for ₦200,000 is depreciated at 10% per annum using the reducing balance method. What is the net book value of the machine at the end of the second year?
questions.e: Year 1: 200,000 x 0.90 = 180,000. Year 2: 180,000 x 0.90 = 162,000. The reducing balance method applies the rate to the net book value, not the original cost, each year.
questions.p: Year 1: 200,000 x 0.90 = 180,000. Year 2: 180,000 x 0.90 = 162,000. Reducing balance dey apply the rate on the balance wey remain, no be the original cost every time.

questions.q: A delivery van owned by Chika Ventures cost ₦120,000 and had accumulated depreciation of ₦80,000 at the date of disposal. The van was sold for ₦50,000. What is the result of this disposal?
questions.e: Net book value = Cost - Accumulated depreciation = 120,000 - 80,000 = 40,000. Since the van was sold for 50,000, which is higher than the net book value, there is a profit of 50,000 - 40,000 = 10,000.
questions.p: Net book value = Cost minus Accumulated depreciation = 120,000 - 80,000 = 40,000. Dem sell the van for 50,000, wey pass the net book value, so na profit of 50,000 - 40,000 = 10,000.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's transport company notices that its buses lose a much bigger portion of their value in the first two years of use than in later years, due to heavy early usage and quick technological wear. Which depreciation method best matches this pattern of value loss?
o: Units of production method based only on distance travelled
questions.e: The reducing balance method charges higher depreciation in the earlier years because it applies a fixed percentage to a reducing net book value, matching assets that lose value quickly at first, such as vehicles.
questions.p: Reducing balance method dey charge higher depreciation for the early years because e dey apply percentage on the balance wey remain, wey still high for early years. This one match assets wey dey lose value fast for beginning, like motor.

questions.q: Okonkwo Enterprises bought a printing machine for ₦300,000 with an estimated useful life of 6 years and no residual value, using the straight line method. The machine was sold after 3 years of use for ₦170,000. What was the result of the disposal?
questions.e: Annual depreciation = 300,000/6 = 50,000. After 3 years, accumulated depreciation = 150,000, so net book value = 300,000 - 150,000 = 150,000. The machine was sold for 170,000, giving a profit of 170,000 - 150,000 = 20,000.
questions.p: Annual depreciation = 300,000/6 = 50,000. After 3 years, accumulated depreciation = 150,000, so net book value = 300,000 - 150,000 = 150,000. Dem sell am for 170,000, so profit = 170,000 - 150,000 = 20,000.

questions.q: When a non-current asset is sold, which journal entry correctly transfers the accumulated depreciation on that asset out of the accumulated depreciation account into the disposal account?
o: Debit Bank account; Credit Accumulated Depreciation account
Debit Accumulated Depreciation account; Credit Disposal account
Debit Disposal account; Credit Accumulated Depreciation account
Debit Asset account; Credit Accumulated Depreciation account
questions.e: To close off accumulated depreciation on disposal, the accumulated depreciation account is debited (to reduce its balance to zero for that asset) and the disposal account is credited with the same amount.
questions.p: To clear the accumulated depreciation when dem sell asset, you go debit Accumulated Depreciation account (make e balance reach zero for that asset) and credit the Disposal account with the same amount.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of preparing a control account in a business's accounting system?
o: To replace the need for keeping individual customers' or suppliers' accounts
To calculate the net profit of the business for the year
To check the arithmetical accuracy of a subsidiary ledger and help locate errors
To record only cash transactions of the business
questions.e: A control account is a summary account that shows the total of all debtors or creditors. Its balance should agree with the total of individual balances in the subsidiary ledger, so it helps to check accuracy and trace errors.
questions.p: Control account na summary account wey show total of all debtors or creditors. Im balance suppose match the total wey dem get for the individual accounts, so e dey help to check mistake.

questions.q: Chief Bello's Sales Ledger Control Account shows: opening debit balance ₦45,000; credit sales ₦120,000; cash received from debtors ₦95,000; discount allowed ₦5,000; returns inward ₦8,000; bad debts written off ₦2,000. What is the closing balance of the account?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit sales - Cash received - Discount allowed - Returns inward - Bad debts = 45,000+120,000-95,000-5,000-8,000-2,000 = ₦55,000.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit sales - Cash wey dem collect - Discount allowed - Returns inward - Bad debt = 45,000+120,000-95,000-5,000-8,000-2,000 = ₦55,000.

questions.q: Nkem Traders' Purchases Ledger Control Account shows: opening credit balance ₦30,000; credit purchases ₦85,000; cash paid to creditors ₦60,000; discount received ₦3,000; returns outward ₦4,000. What is the closing balance of the account?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit purchases - Cash paid - Discount received - Returns outward = 30,000+85,000-60,000-3,000-4,000 = ₦48,000.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit purchases - Cash wey dem pay - Discount wey dem receive - Returns outward = 30,000+85,000-60,000-3,000-4,000 = ₦48,000.

questions.q: In the Sales Ledger Control Account, which of the following items is correctly recorded on the credit side?
o: Opening balance of debtors brought forward
questions.e: Cash received from debtors reduces the amount owed, so it is a credit entry in the Sales Ledger Control Account. Credit sales, dishonoured cheques and opening debtor balances all increase debtors and are debit entries.
questions.p: Cash wey debtor pay dey reduce wetin e owe, so na credit entry for Sales Ledger Control Account. Credit sales, dishonoured cheques and opening balance dey increase debtors so na debit entries.

questions.q: Oga Emeka's Sales Ledger Control Account shows: opening balance ₦60,000; credit sales ₦200,000; cash received from debtors ₦180,000; discount allowed ₦6,000; returns inward ₦10,000; closing balance ₦58,000. What amount of bad debts was written off during the period?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening + Sales - Cash received - Discount - Returns - Bad debts. So 58,000 = 60,000+200,000-180,000-6,000-10,000-Bad debts, giving 58,000 = 64,000 - Bad debts, so Bad debts = ₦6,000.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening + Sales - Cash - Discount - Returns - Bad debt. So 58,000 = 60,000+200,000-180,000-6,000-10,000-Bad debt, e go be 58,000 = 64,000 - Bad debt, so Bad debt na ₦6,000.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a self-balancing ledger system?
o: A system where control accounts are prepared only once, at the end of the business's life
A system where only one ledger is maintained for the whole business
A system where subsidiary books such as the sales day book are no longer required
A system where each ledger (e.g. sales, purchases, general) contains its own control account so that each ledger can be proved to balance independently of the others
questions.e: In a self-balancing ledger system, each ledger has a control account that summarises the double entries affecting it, allowing each ledger to be balanced on its own without needing the other ledgers. This helps in locating errors quickly.
questions.p: For self-balancing ledger system, each ledger get im own control account wey summarize the entries wey affect am, so each ledger fit balance on im own without needing the other ledgers. Dis dey help to quick find mistake.

questions.q: Mrs Chidinma Okafor owes a business ₦18,000 as recorded in the Sales Ledger, and the business also owes her ₦18,000 for goods she supplied, as recorded in the Purchases Ledger, since she is both a customer and a supplier. The two parties agree to set off ₦12,000 of this mutual debt through a contra entry. What amount will appear on the credit side of the Sales Ledger Control Account as the contra entry?
questions.e: A contra entry sets off a debtor balance against a creditor balance for the same person. The amount actually set off is ₦12,000, so this is the figure credited in the Sales Ledger Control Account (reducing debtors) and debited in the Purchases Ledger Control Account (reducing creditors).
questions.p: Contra entry na to set off debtor balance against creditor balance for the same person. The amount wey dem set off na ₦12,000, so na im dem go credit for Sales Ledger Control Account (e dey reduce debtors) and debit am for Purchases Ledger Control Account (e dey reduce creditors).

questions.q: The balance carried down on the Sales Ledger Control Account should normally agree with which of the following?
o: The closing balance shown on the bank statement
The total of the balances extracted from the individual debtors' accounts in the sales ledger
The net profit figure shown in the statement of profit or loss
The total of the balances in the purchases ledger
questions.e: The Sales Ledger Control Account is a summary of all individual debtors' accounts, so its closing balance must equal the total of the balances of individual debtors' accounts in the sales ledger. If they differ, there is an error somewhere.
questions.p: Sales Ledger Control Account na summary of all the individual debtors' accounts, so im closing balance suppose match the total of the individual debtors' balances for sales ledger. If dem no match, e mean say mistake dey somewhere.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the single entry/incomplete records system of bookkeeping?
o: A system used exclusively by multinational companies instead of double entry
A system in which only the owner's capital account is updated at year end
A system in which some transactions are not fully recorded, so not all accounts needed to prepare a trial balance are available
A system in which every transaction is recorded twice, as debit and credit, in full compliance with double entry principles
questions.e: Incomplete records (single entry) means the trader has not kept full double entry books, so some accounts (like a complete trial balance) cannot be prepared directly. The accountant must reconstruct missing figures using available documents like cash books and bank statements.
questions.p: Incomplete record na when the business no keep full double entry book, so some account no dey complete to make trial balance straight. Accountant go use the small info wey dey there (like cash book) to find the missing figures.

questions.q: A trader who does not keep proper double entry records wants to determine his capital at the start of the trading year. Which document should he prepare?
questions.e: A statement of affairs lists all assets and liabilities to find capital (Assets minus Liabilities) when full records are not kept. It serves the same purpose as a balance sheet in a single entry system.
questions.p: Statement of affairs na the list wey show all assets and liabilities so dem fit calculate capital (Assets minus Liabilities) when the business no get full record. E dey work like balance sheet for single entry system.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa does not keep complete accounting records for his provisions business. On 1 January 2023, his assets and liabilities were as follows: Premises N800,000; Stock of goods N150,000; Trade debtors N90,000; Cash at bank N60,000; Trade creditors N70,000; Bank loan N200,000. Using the statement of affairs method, calculate his capital as at 1 January 2023.
questions.p: Total assets na 800,000+150,000+90,000+60,000 = 1,100,000. Total liabilities na 70,000+200,000 = 270,000. Capital na Assets minus Liabilities = 1,100,000 - 270,000 = 830,000.

questions.q: Mrs Chidinma's business had an opening capital of N500,000 and a closing capital of N650,000 for the year ended 31 December 2023. During the year, she introduced additional capital of N40,000 into the business and withdrew N30,000 for personal use. Calculate the net profit made by the business for the year.
questions.e: Profit = (Closing capital + Drawings) - (Opening capital + Additional capital) = (650,000+30,000) - (500,000+40,000) = 680,000 - 540,000 = 140,000. Drawings reduce capital so they are added back, while new capital introduced is removed before comparing with the opening figure.
questions.p: Profit na (Closing capital + Drawings) minus (Opening capital + New capital) = (650,000+30,000) - (500,000+40,000) = 680,000 - 540,000 = 140,000. Since drawings dey reduce capital, we add am back, and we remove the new capital wey she bring before we compare.

questions.q: The following information was extracted from the books of Oga Peters Stores, which keeps incomplete records: Trade debtors at 1 January 2023, N45,000; Trade debtors at 31 December 2023, N60,000; Cash received from debtors during the year, N380,000; Discount allowed, N5,000; Returns inwards, N8,000. Using the total debtors account, calculate the credit sales for the year.
questions.e: In the total debtors account: Opening debtors + Credit sales = Cash received + Discount allowed + Returns inwards + Closing debtors. So Credit sales = 380,000+5,000+8,000+60,000-45,000 = 408,000.
questions.p: For total debtors account: Opening debtors + Credit sales = Cash wey dem receive + Discount allowed + Returns inwards + Closing debtors. So Credit sales = 380,000+5,000+8,000+60,000-45,000 = 408,000.

questions.q: The following information relates to Amaka Ventures, which operates a single entry system: Trade creditors at 1 January 2023, N72,000; Trade creditors at 31 December 2023, N95,000; Cash paid to creditors during the year, N460,000; Discount received, N10,000; Returns outwards, N12,000. Using the total creditors account, calculate the credit purchases for the year.
questions.e: In the total creditors account: Opening creditors + Credit purchases = Cash paid + Discount received + Returns outwards + Closing creditors. So Credit purchases = 460,000+10,000+12,000+95,000-72,000 = 505,000.
questions.p: For total creditors account: Opening creditors + Credit purchases = Cash wey dem pay + Discount received + Returns outwards + Closing creditors. So Credit purchases = 460,000+10,000+12,000+95,000-72,000 = 505,000.

questions.q: At 1 January 2023, Mrs Bello's business had total assets of N920,000 and total liabilities of N220,000. At 31 December 2023, her total assets were N1,000,000 and total liabilities were N170,000. During the year, she introduced additional capital of N50,000 and the business earned a net profit of N160,000. Calculate the total drawings made during the year.
questions.e: Opening capital = 920,000-220,000 = 700,000. Closing capital = 1,000,000-170,000 = 830,000. Closing capital = Opening capital + Additional capital + Profit - Drawings, so Drawings = (700,000+50,000+160,000) - 830,000 = 910,000-830,000 = 80,000.
questions.p: Opening capital = 920,000-220,000 = 700,000. Closing capital = 1,000,000-170,000 = 830,000. Since Closing capital = Opening capital + New capital + Profit - Drawings, Drawings = (700,000+50,000+160,000) - 830,000 = 910,000-830,000 = 80,000.

questions.q: A trader sells goods at a mark-up of 25% on cost. If the cost of goods sold for the year was N240,000, calculate the value of sales for the year.
questions.e: Mark-up of 25% on cost means Sales = Cost + 25% of Cost = 240,000 x 1.25 = 300,000. This is different from a 25% margin on sales, which would give a different (higher) sales figure.
questions.p: Mark-up of 25% on cost mean Sales = Cost + 25% of Cost = 240,000 x 1.25 = 300,000. E different from 25% margin on sales wey for give bigger sales figure.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of preparing a manufacturing account in a set of final accounts?
o: To determine the cost of production of goods manufactured during the period
To record the day-to-day cash transactions of the business
To show the financial position of the business at a particular date
To calculate the net profit of the business for the year
questions.e: The manufacturing account is prepared by firms that make their own goods to find out the total cost of producing those goods before they are transferred to the trading account. It is not the same as the profit and loss account or the balance sheet.
questions.p: Dem dey use manufacturing account to find out how much e cost to produce the goods for that period. E no be profit and loss account or balance sheet, na just to sabi production cost.

questions.q: Which of the following items is NOT included when computing the prime cost in a manufacturing account?
o: Direct expenses such as royalties paid per unit produced
questions.e: Prime cost = direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses. Factory rent is an indirect cost, so it is treated as a factory overhead, not part of prime cost.
questions.p: Prime cost na direct material add direct labour add direct expenses. Factory rent na overhead, e no dey enter prime cost at all.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's furniture factory in Kano recorded the following for the year: direct materials consumed ₦180,000, direct labour ₦95,000, and direct expenses (royalty paid per unit produced) ₦15,000. Calculate the prime cost.
questions.e: Prime cost = direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses = 180,000 + 95,000 + 15,000 = ₦290,000. All three direct cost elements must be added together.
questions.p: Prime cost na material add labour add expenses: 180,000 + 95,000 + 15,000 = ₦290,000. You must add all three direct costs make e complete.

questions.q: Opeyemi Ventures, a soap manufacturing company in Lagos, had an opening stock of raw materials of ₦60,000, purchased raw materials worth ₦420,000 during the year, and had a closing stock of raw materials of ₦90,000. Calculate the cost of raw materials consumed.
questions.e: Cost of materials consumed = Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock = 60,000 + 420,000 - 90,000 = ₦390,000. You must deduct the closing stock because it was not used up during the year.
questions.p: Material wey dem use = Opening stock + Purchase - Closing stock = 60,000 + 420,000 - 90,000 = ₦390,000. Make sure you minus the closing stock because dem never use am.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct example of a direct expense in a manufacturing account?
o: Royalty paid to a patent owner based on the number of units produced
questions.e: A direct expense is a cost directly linked to the production of each unit, such as royalties paid per unit manufactured. Rent, depreciation and supervisor salary are indirect costs classified as factory overheads.
questions.p: Direct expense na cost wey dey attach straight to every unit wey dem produce, like royalty wey dem pay per unit. Rent, depreciation and supervisor salary na overhead, e no direct.

questions.q: Chinedu Industries Ltd compiled the following figures for the year: Prime cost ₦260,000; Factory overheads ₦140,000; Opening work-in-progress ₦40,000; Closing work-in-progress ₦60,000. Calculate the cost of production.
questions.e: Cost of production = Prime cost + Factory overheads + Opening WIP - Closing WIP = 260,000 + 140,000 + 40,000 - 60,000 = ₦380,000. The opening WIP is added because it was finished this year, while closing WIP is removed because it is still unfinished.
questions.p: Cost of production = Prime cost + Overheads + Opening WIP - Closing WIP = 260,000+140,000+40,000-60,000 = ₦380,000. Opening WIP don finish so you add am, closing WIP never finish so you minus am.

questions.q: Yusuf Manufacturing Company produced goods at a total cost of production of ₦720,000. These finished goods were transferred to the trading account at a market (transfer) value of ₦900,000. Calculate the factory profit on the goods produced.
questions.e: Factory profit = Market value (transfer price) - Cost of production = 900,000 - 720,000 = ₦180,000. This profit is credited to the manufacturing account and shown separately in the profit and loss account.
questions.p: Factory profit = Market value minus Cost of production = 900,000 - 720,000 = ₦180,000. Na dis profit dem go credit for manufacturing account and show am separately for profit and loss account.

questions.q: A manufacturing company transfers its finished goods from the factory to the warehouse at a mark-up of 25% on cost. At the end of the year, the closing stock of finished goods in the warehouse, valued at transfer price, was ₦250,000. Calculate the provision for unrealised profit (stock reserve) to be created on this closing stock.
questions.e: A 25% mark-up on cost means profit is 1/5 of the transfer price (since transfer price = cost x 1.25, profit/transfer price = 0.25/1.25 = 1/5). So unrealised profit = 250,000 x 1/5 = ₦50,000. A common mistake is to take 25% straight of 250,000, which wrongly treats mark-up as margin.
questions.p: 25% mark-up on cost mean say profit na 1/5 of the transfer price (because transfer price = cost x 1.25, so profit/transfer price = 0.25/1.25 = 1/5). So unrealised profit = 250,000 x 1/5 = ₦50,000. If you just take 25% of 250,000 straight, you don mix mark-up with margin, na wrong way.

questions.q: Which financial statement prepared by a not-for-profit organisation is a summary of all cash and bank receipts and payments during a financial year, and is similar in structure to a cash book with a debit and credit side?
questions.e: The Receipts and Payments Account records only cash/bank movements for the year, both capital and revenue items, without adjusting for accruals. It opens with the cash balance brought forward and closes with the balance carried down.
questions.p: Na Receipts and Payments Account dem dey use record only cash wey enter and cash wey comot for the year, e no de adjust for wetin dem owe or wetin dem don pay before. E be like cash book wey show opening and closing balance.

questions.q: In the final accounts of a social club, the amount that corresponds to the 'capital' of a sole trader, representing accumulated surpluses and capital receipts over the years, is called the:
questions.e: Since a not-for-profit organisation has no owner contributing capital, the equivalent balancing figure in its statement of financial position is called the Accumulated Fund, built up from surpluses, donations and capital receipts over time.
questions.p: Because club no get owner wey put capital, dem dey call the balancing figure for their balance sheet 'Accumulated Fund'. Na from surplus, donation and capital money wey don enter years dem build am.

questions.q: Oke-Ira Social Club's statement of affairs at the start of the year showed: Clubhouse ₦500,000; Furniture ₦80,000; Cash at bank ₦20,000; and Subscriptions received in advance ₦10,000 (a liability). What was the club's Accumulated Fund at that date?
questions.e: Accumulated Fund = Total Assets minus Total Liabilities = (500,000 + 80,000 + 20,000) − 10,000 = 600,000 − 10,000 = ₦590,000. This is the opening capital balance for the club.
questions.p: Accumulated Fund na Total Assets minus Total Liabilities: (500,000 + 80,000 + 20,000) minus 10,000 = 600,000 minus 10,000 = ₦590,000.

questions.q: Ajayi Sports Club's cash book showed subscriptions received of ₦150,000 during the year. At the start of the year, ₦12,000 was owed by members and ₦5,000 had been paid in advance for the current year. At the end of the year, ₦18,000 was still owed by members and ₦8,000 had been paid in advance for next year. What is the subscription income to be shown in the Income and Expenditure Account for the year?
questions.e: Income = Cash received − Opening owing + Closing owing + Opening advance − Closing advance = 150,000 − 12,000 + 18,000 + 5,000 − 8,000 = ₦153,000. This adjusts cash receipts to the true amount earned for the year.
