questions.p: Income wey belong this year = Cash wey enter minus wetin dem owe before plus wetin dem still owe now plus advance wey dem pay before minus advance wey dem pay now: 150,000 − 12,000 + 18,000 + 5,000 − 8,000 = ₦153,000.

questions.q: Idera Tennis Club's constitution states that entrance fees paid by new members are to be treated as capital receipts, not revenue income. How should the entrance fees received during the year be treated in the club's final accounts?
o: Credited to the Income and Expenditure Account as ordinary income
Deducted from subscriptions received in the Receipts and Payments Account
Added directly to the Accumulated Fund in the statement of financial position
Shown as a current liability in the statement of financial position
questions.e: Where the constitution classifies entrance fees as capital in nature, they are not passed through the Income and Expenditure Account; instead they are added straight to the Accumulated Fund, increasing the club's long-term reserve.
questions.p: Since the club rules talk say entrance fee na capital money, e no go enter Income and Expenditure Account; instead, dem go add am straight to the Accumulated Fund for the balance sheet.

questions.q: Falconry Social Club's Receipts and Payments Account for the year showed: Subscriptions received ₦300,000; Donations received ₦50,000; Rent paid ₦80,000; Salaries paid ₦120,000; Stationery paid ₦10,000. Additional information: Subscriptions owing (not yet received) at year end ₦5,000; Depreciation on equipment for the year ₦20,000. There were no subscriptions in advance. What is the surplus of income over expenditure for the year?
questions.e: Income = Subscriptions (300,000+5,000 owing)=305,000 + Donations 50,000 = 355,000. Expenditure = Rent 80,000 + Salaries 120,000 + Stationery 10,000 + Depreciation 20,000 = 230,000. Surplus = 355,000 − 230,000 = ₦125,000. Depreciation is a non-cash expense that must still be charged even though it is not in the cash account.
questions.p: Income = Subscriptions (300,000+5,000 wey dem still owe)=305,000 plus Donation 50,000 = 355,000. Expenditure = Rent 80,000 + Salary 120,000 + Stationery 10,000 + Depreciation 20,000 = 230,000. Surplus = 355,000 minus 230,000 = ₦125,000. Even though depreciation no be cash, dem still must charge am.

questions.q: Greenfield Recreation Club runs a bar for its members. During the year: Bar sales were ₦400,000; Opening stock of drinks was ₦30,000; Purchases of drinks were ₦250,000; Closing stock of drinks was ₦40,000; Bar wages paid were ₦25,000. What was the net profit made on the bar for the year?
questions.e: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Closing stock = 30,000+250,000−40,000 = 240,000. Gross bar profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold = 400,000−240,000 = 160,000. Net bar profit = Gross profit − Bar wages = 160,000−25,000 = ₦135,000.
questions.p: Cost of goods wey dem sell = Opening stock + Purchase minus Closing stock = 30,000+250,000 minus 40,000 = 240,000. Gross profit = Sales minus that cost = 400,000 minus 240,000 = 160,000. Net profit = Gross profit minus bar wages = 160,000 minus 25,000 = ₦135,000.

questions.q: Unity Club received ₦100,000 as life membership fees from a member during the year. The club's policy is to spread life membership fees over 10 years in the Income and Expenditure Account. What amount should be credited to the Income and Expenditure Account for the current year in respect of this fee?
questions.e: Since the club spreads the ₦100,000 life membership fee equally over 10 years, the amount credited each year is 100,000 divided by 10 = ₦10,000. The remaining balance is carried forward as a liability (deferred income) in the statement of financial position.
questions.p: Since the club dey share the ₦100,000 life membership fee for 10 years, the money wey go enter Income and Expenditure Account every year na 100,000 divide by 10 = ₦10,000. The remaining balance go dey carry forward as liability for balance sheet.

questions.q: Which of the following documents normally contains the terms and conditions guiding the operations of a partnership business, including the profit-sharing ratio, capital contributions, and interest on capital or drawings agreed upon by the partners?
questions.e: The partnership deed is the legal document that spells out the rules guiding a partnership, such as capital, profit sharing, salaries and interest. The other options relate to companies or trusts, not partnerships.
questions.p: Partnership deed na di paper wey carry all di rules wey go guide di partnership business, like how dem go share capital and profit. Di oda options na for companies or trust, dem no concern partnership.

questions.q: Chidi and Ngozi formed a partnership business but did not sign any written partnership agreement. According to the general rule guiding partnership accounts in the absence of a partnership agreement, how should profits and losses be shared between them?
o: According to the time each devoted to the business
In the ratio of their capital contributions
In the ratio of 2:1 in favour of the partner who contributed more capital
questions.e: Where there is no partnership agreement, the law assumes all partners share profits and losses equally, regardless of capital contributed or time spent working.
questions.p: If no partnership agreement dey, di law say make dem share profit and loss equally, no matter di capital wey each one bring or di time wey dem spend for di business.

questions.q: Tunde and Bisi are partners in a business. Tunde contributed capital of ₦200,000 while Bisi contributed ₦150,000. Their agreement allows 10% per annum interest on capital before any sharing of profit. What is Bisi's interest on capital for the year?
questions.e: Interest on capital is calculated as capital x rate. For Bisi: ₦150,000 x 10/100 = ₦15,000.
questions.p: Interest on capital na capital multiply by rate. For Bisi: ₦150,000 x 10/100 = ₦15,000.

questions.q: In the appropriation account of Musa and Hassan's partnership, net profit for the year was ₦120,000. Musa is entitled to an annual salary of ₦20,000, and total interest on capital for both partners amounted to ₦10,000. The remaining (residual) profit is shared equally between Musa and Hassan. What is Hassan's share of the residual profit?
questions.e: Residual profit = ₦120,000 - ₦20,000 (salary) - ₦10,000 (interest) = ₦90,000. Shared equally between the two partners gives Hassan ₦90,000/2 = ₦45,000.
questions.p: Di remaining profit be ₦120,000 - ₦20,000 (salary) - ₦10,000 (interest) = ₦90,000. Dem go share am equally, so Hassan go collect ₦90,000/2 = ₦45,000.

questions.q: A partnership's net profits for the last three years were ₦40,000, ₦50,000 and ₦60,000 respectively. If goodwill is valued at two years' purchase of the average profit, what is the value of goodwill?
questions.e: Average profit = (40,000+50,000+60,000)/3 = ₦50,000. Goodwill at two years' purchase = 2 x 50,000 = ₦100,000.
questions.p: Average profit = (40,000+50,000+60,000)/3 = ₦50,000. Goodwill wey be two years purchase = 2 x 50,000 = ₦100,000.

questions.q: At the beginning of the year, Funke's current account had a credit balance of ₦30,000. During the year, she was credited with interest on capital of ₦5,000 and a share of profit of ₦25,000, while she was debited with drawings of ₦15,000 and interest on drawings of ₦2,000. What is the closing balance on Funke's current account?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening balance + credits - debits = 30,000 + 5,000 + 25,000 - 15,000 - 2,000 = ₦43,000. Current accounts record such day-to-day movements, unlike the fixed capital account.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening balance + credit items - debit items = 30,000 + 5,000 + 25,000 - 15,000 - 2,000 = ₦43,000. Na current account dem dey use record all dis small-small movements, no be capital account.

questions.q: A partner withdrew a total of ₦60,000 from the business evenly throughout the year for personal use. The partnership charges interest on drawings at 5% per annum, calculated on the assumption that the drawings were spread evenly over the year (average period of 6 months). What is the interest on drawings?
questions.e: Since drawings were spread evenly, the average period used is 6 months. Interest = ₦60,000 x 5/100 x 6/12 = ₦1,500.
questions.p: Since dem spread di drawings evenly, dem go use average period of 6 months. Interest = ₦60,000 x 5/100 x 6/12 = ₦1,500.

questions.q: What is a debenture in company accounts?
o: A reserve created from retained profits
A discount allowed on issue of shares
A loan to a company carrying a fixed rate of interest
A share that carries voting rights
questions.e: A debenture is a form of long-term borrowing by a company. It carries a fixed rate of interest which must be paid whether the company makes profit or not, unlike dividends on shares.
questions.p: Debenture na loan wey company collect, and e dey carry fixed interest rate. Dem must pay the interest even if company no make profit, unlike dividend wey depend on profit.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a capital reserve in a company's accounts?
questions.e: Share premium arises from capital transactions (issuing shares above nominal value), not from trading profit, so it is a capital reserve. General reserve, retained earnings and dividend equalization reserve are all revenue reserves created from trading profits.
questions.p: Share premium na money wey company collect when e sell shares pass the nominal value, e no come from trading profit, so na capital reserve. The other three na revenue reserves wey come from profit.

questions.q: Afrilink Plc issued 50,000 ordinary shares of ₦2 each at a premium of ₦0.50 per share. All the shares were fully subscribed and paid for. Calculate the total amount received by the company from this issue.
questions.e: Each share is sold for the nominal value plus premium: ₦2 + ₦0.50 = ₦2.50. Total received = 50,000 x ₦2.50 = ₦125,000.
questions.p: Each share dem sell am na nominal value plus premium: ₦2 + ₦0.50 = ₦2.50. So total wey company collect na 50,000 x ₦2.50 = ₦125,000.

questions.q: Bayelsa Textiles Ltd has ₦200,000 of 10% debentures in issue. Calculate the amount of annual interest the company must pay to debenture holders.
questions.e: Interest on debentures is a fixed percentage of the nominal value of the debentures. 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000 payable yearly regardless of profit level.
questions.p: Debenture interest na fixed percentage of the nominal value. 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000 wey dem go pay every year, profit or no profit.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes a key difference between preference shares and ordinary shares?
o: Preference shares carry voting rights equal to ordinary shares
Preference shareholders are paid after ordinary shareholders when the company winds up
Preference share dividend fluctuates with profit exactly like ordinary share dividend
Preference shareholders have priority in dividend payment over ordinary shareholders
questions.e: Preference shares usually carry a fixed dividend rate and must be paid before any dividend is given to ordinary shareholders. Ordinary shareholders only receive dividend from what remains, and their dividend varies with profit.
questions.p: Preference shares dey get fixed dividend rate and dem go pay am first before ordinary shareholders. Ordinary shareholders go collect wetin remain, and their own dividend dey change according to profit.

questions.q: A company forfeited 1,000 shares of ₦5 each on which ₦3 per share had been received, including a premium of ₦0.50 per share which had already been fully received before forfeiture. The forfeited shares were later reissued at ₦4 per share, fully paid. Calculate the amount transferred to capital reserve after the reissue.
questions.e: Amount forfeited excluding premium = (₦3 - ₦0.50) x 1,000 = ₦2,500. Discount given on reissue = (₦5 - ₦4) x 1,000 = ₦1,000. Balance to capital reserve = ₦2,500 - ₦1,000 = ₦1,500.
questions.p: Amount wey dem forfeit (without premium) = (₦3 - ₦0.50) x 1,000 = ₦2,500. Discount wey dem give for reissue = (₦5 - ₦4) x 1,000 = ₦1,000. Wetin remain go capital reserve = ₦2,500 - ₦1,000 = ₦1,500.

questions.q: Delta Breweries Plc has 20,000 8% preference shares of ₦10 each and 100,000 ordinary shares of ₦5 each. The profit available for distribution is ₦150,000. After paying the preference dividend in full, the directors share the remaining profit equally among the ordinary shares. Calculate the dividend per ordinary share.
questions.e: Preference dividend = 8% x ₦10 x 20,000 = ₦16,000. Remaining profit = ₦150,000 - ₦16,000 = ₦134,000. Dividend per ordinary share = ₦134,000 / 100,000 shares = ₦1.34.
questions.p: Preference dividend = 8% x ₦10 x 20,000 = ₦16,000. Wetin remain = ₦150,000 - ₦16,000 = ₦134,000. Dividend for each ordinary share = ₦134,000 / 100,000 = ₦1.34.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a general reserve in a company's financial statements?
o: Amount received above the nominal value of shares
Reserve that can only be used to pay dividends to preference shareholders
Reserve created specifically to redeem debentures
Profit set aside for unspecified future use, not tied to any particular purpose
questions.e: A general reserve is part of retained profit that directors set aside for the overall strengthening of the company, not for any specific named purpose. This makes it different from specific reserves such as a debenture redemption reserve.
questions.p: General reserve na part of profit wey directors set aside to make company strong, e no be for any particular purpose. E different from specific reserve like the one wey dem use to redeem debenture.

questions.q: In accounting, what is the main purpose of preparing departmental accounts for a business with several departments?
o: To show total profit of the whole business only
To calculate value added tax payable
To show the profit or loss made by each department
To avoid preparing a trial balance
questions.e: Departmental accounts are prepared so that management can see how much profit or loss each department is making separately, which helps in decision making. It is not about avoiding the trial balance or calculating tax.
questions.p: Dem dey prepare departmental accounts so management go fit see how much profit or loss each department dey make one by one. E no be about trial balance or tax.

questions.q: Chidinma Stores has three departments sharing one shop building. Which basis is most appropriate for apportioning rent and rates among the departments?
o: Floor area occupied by each department
Number of employees in each department
questions.e: Rent and rates are charges for occupying space, so they should be shared according to the floor area each department occupies. Sharing by sales or staff number would not reflect actual space usage.
questions.p: Rent and rates na charge for the space wey dem dey use, so na floor area each department dey occupy go determine how dem go share am. To use sales or staff number no go correct.

questions.q: Zainab Enterprises has two departments, X and Y, sharing the same premises. Department X occupies 600 square metres and Department Y occupies 400 square metres of floor space. Total rent for the year is ₦50,000, apportioned on the basis of floor area. What is Department X's share of the rent?
questions.e: Total floor area is 600 + 400 = 1000 sqm. Department X's share = (600/1000) x ₦50,000 = ₦30,000.

questions.q: When apportioning sales commission paid to salesmen among the departments of a business, which basis is most suitable?
o: Number of employees in each department
Cost of goods purchased by each department
Floor area occupied by each department
questions.e: Sales commission is earned based on how much is sold, so it should be shared according to the sales value made by each department. Floor area or staff number does not reflect selling effort.
questions.p: Sales commission dey based on how much dem sell, so e suppose share am based on sales value of each department. Floor area or staff number no relate to selling work.

questions.q: Obi Enterprises, based in Onitsha, sent goods costing ₦200,000 at cost price to its Aba branch during the year. The branch sold all the goods for ₦280,000 cash and incurred branch running expenses of ₦30,000. There was no opening or closing stock at the branch. Using a simple branch account at cost, what is the branch profit for the year?
questions.e: Branch profit = Sales - Cost of goods sent - Branch expenses = ₦280,000 - ₦200,000 - ₦30,000 = ₦50,000. Since there is no stock left, the whole ₦200,000 goods sent is treated as cost of sales.
questions.p: Branch profit = Sales - Cost of goods wey dem send - Branch expenses = ₦280,000 - ₦200,000 - ₦30,000 = ₦50,000. Since no stock remain, all the ₦200,000 na cost of sales.

questions.q: A head office invoices goods to its branch at cost plus 25%, so that the invoice price always includes a mark-up for unrealised profit. During the year, goods invoiced to the branch at invoice price amounted to ₦150,000. What is the amount of unrealised profit (loading) included in this invoice price?
questions.e: Since cost plus 25% equals the invoice price, the loading fraction of the invoice price is 25/125 = 1/5. Loading = 1/5 x ₦150,000 = ₦30,000.
questions.p: Since cost plus 25% na the invoice price, the loading wey dey inside invoice price na 25/125 = 1/5. Loading = 1/5 x ₦150,000 = ₦30,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a joint venture in accounting?
o: A temporary partnership formed by two or more persons to carry out a specific business venture and share profits and losses
A branch of a company located in another location
A permanent partnership formed to carry on a continuing business for many years
A department within an organisation handling exports only
questions.e: A joint venture is set up for a specific, short-term business deal, after which it ends, unlike a permanent partnership which continues indefinitely. It is also different from a branch or a department, which are parts of one single organisation.
questions.p: Joint venture na temporary arrangement wey two or more people form just to do one specific business deal, and e go end after. E different from permanent partnership, branch, or department wey be part of one organisation.

questions.q: Public sector accounting can best be described as the process of:
o: recording, classifying and reporting the financial transactions of government and its agencies
recording only the profit made by private limited liability companies
preparing final accounts for sole traders and partnerships
computing personal income tax payable by individual workers
questions.e: Public sector accounting deals with how government ministries, departments and agencies record, classify and report their revenues and expenditures. It is different from private sector accounting which focuses on profit-making businesses.
questions.p: Public sector accounting na how government ministries and agencies dey record, classify and report their money matters. E different from private company accounting wey dey focus on profit.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a normal source of revenue to the Nigerian government?
o: Grants-in-aid from foreign governments or agencies
Dividend earned personally by a private citizen from his own shares in a company
Taxes collected from citizens and companies
Royalties from crude oil and mineral resources
questions.e: Taxes, royalties and grants-in-aid are all recognised government revenue sources. A private citizen's personal dividend income belongs to him, not to government, so it is not government revenue.
questions.p: Tax, royalty and grants na correct government money. But if person get im own shares for company and e dey collect dividend, na im personal money, e no be government revenue.

questions.q: The annual law passed by the National Assembly which authorises the government to spend money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for a given fiscal year is called the:
questions.e: The Appropriation Act is the annual budget law that gives government legal approval to withdraw and spend money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund. Without it, spending would be unauthorised.
questions.p: Na Appropriation Act be di yearly law wey National Assembly dey pass make government fit spend money from Consolidated Revenue Fund. Without am, government no get permission to spend.

questions.q: Which government fund holds all revenues collected by the Federal Government except those specifically allocated by law to other funds such as the Development Fund?
questions.e: The Consolidated Revenue Fund is the main pool into which all federal government revenue is paid, except amounts that the law directs into other special funds like the Development Fund or Contingency Fund.
questions.p: Consolidated Revenue Fund na di main place where all federal government money dey enter, except di ones wey law don already arrange make e go anoda fund like Development Fund.

questions.q: In government accounting, capital expenditure refers mainly to spending on:
o: construction of new roads, bridges and purchase of long-term assets
salaries and wages of civil servants
payment of pensions and gratuities to retirees
questions.e: Capital expenditure is spending that creates or adds long-lasting assets for government, such as new roads, bridges, buildings and equipment that will be used for many years. Salaries, maintenance and pensions are recurrent expenditure.
questions.p: Capital expenditure na money wey government dey spend to build new road, bridge, or buy long-term assets wey go last for many years. Salary, maintenance and pension na recurrent expenditure.

questions.q: The Federal Government of Nigeria approved a total budget of ₦12,000,000,000 for a fiscal year. If recurrent expenditure takes up 65% of the total budget, how much naira is allocated to capital expenditure?
questions.e: Capital expenditure share = 100% - 65% = 35%. So capital expenditure = 35% of ₦12,000,000,000 = 0.35 x 12,000,000,000 = ₦4,200,000,000.
questions.p: Capital expenditure percentage na 100% - 65% = 35%. So e go be 0.35 x ₦12,000,000,000 = ₦4,200,000,000.

questions.q: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) policy was introduced by the Nigerian government mainly to:
o: reduce the amount of tax paid by government parastatals
allow each government agency to keep separate commercial bank accounts for its revenue
consolidate all government revenues into one central account for easier monitoring and control
increase the number of bank accounts operated by ministries
questions.e: TSA brings all government revenue from different ministries and agencies into one unified account at the Central Bank. This makes it easier for government to monitor cash flow, prevent leakages and improve accountability.
questions.p: TSA na policy wey dey gather all government money from different ministries put am for one account for Central Bank. Dis one make am easy to monitor money, stop leakage, and improve accountability.

questions.q: Which method of stock (inventory) valuation assumes that the goods bought first are also the goods sold first, so that the closing stock consists of the most recently purchased items?
questions.e: FIFO (First-In-First-Out) means the earliest purchased goods are sold first, so what remains in stock are the newest purchases.
questions.p: FIFO mean say the goods wey you buy first na im you go sell first, so the ones wey remain na the latest ones wey you buy.

questions.q: During a period of continuously rising prices, which stock valuation method will produce the LOWEST value for closing stock?
questions.e: LIFO assumes the most recently bought (higher-priced) goods are sold first, leaving the older, cheaper goods in stock, so closing stock value is lowest when prices are rising.
questions.p: LIFO dey assume say the latest goods wey cost pass na im dem sell first, so the old cheap ones remain for store, dat na why closing stock go small pass.

questions.q: Adaeze's shop had the following stock movements for rice bags in January: Opening stock was 100 bags at ₦50 each. On 10th January she bought 150 bags at ₦60 each. On 20th January she sold 180 bags. Using the FIFO method, what is the value of the closing stock at the end of January?
questions.e: Total bags = 100+150 = 250. After selling 180, 70 bags remain. Under FIFO, the 180 sold come from the oldest stock first: all 100 opening bags plus 80 bags from the new purchase, leaving 70 bags from the ₦60 purchase. Closing stock = 70 x ₦60 = ₦4,200.
questions.p: Total bags na 250, she sell 180, so 70 remain. Under FIFO, the 180 wey she sell na the old 100 bags plus 80 from the new batch, so wetin remain na 70 bags from the ₦60 batch. 70 x ₦60 = ₦4,200.

questions.q: Chinedu's provision store recorded the following for sugar during March: Opening stock was 200 bags at ₦40 each. On 15th March he bought 100 bags at ₦45 each. On 25th March he sold 250 bags. Using the LIFO method, what is the value of the closing stock at the end of March?
questions.e: Total bags = 200+100 = 300. After selling 250, 50 bags remain. Under LIFO, the 250 sold come from the newest stock first: all 100 bags from the March purchase plus 150 bags from the opening stock, leaving 50 bags from the opening stock. Closing stock = 50 x ₦40 = ₦2,000.
questions.p: Total bags na 300, 250 don sell, so 50 remain. Under LIFO, the 250 wey sell na the new 100 bags plus 150 from the opening stock, so the 50 wey remain na from opening stock. 50 x ₦40 = ₦2,000.

questions.q: A trader's stock record for cartons of tomato paste in April shows: Opening stock 50 cartons at ₦80 each, and a purchase on 10th April of 150 cartons at ₦90 each. On 20th April, 120 cartons were sold. Using the weighted average cost method (calculated once before the sale), what is the value of the closing stock?
questions.e: Weighted average cost = (50x80 + 150x90) / 200 = 17,500/200 = ₦87.5 per carton. Closing stock units = 50+150-120 = 80. Closing stock value = 80 x 87.5 = ₦7,000.
questions.p: Weighted average cost = (50x80 + 150x90)/200 = 17,500/200 = ₦87.5 per carton. Wetin remain na 80 cartons (50+150-120). So closing stock = 80 x 87.5 = ₦7,000.

questions.q: Prices of goods have been rising steadily throughout the year. Which statement correctly describes the effect of FIFO compared to LIFO on a trader's reported profit for the period?
o: FIFO gives a lower profit than LIFO because recent, higher costs are matched against sales
LIFO gives higher profit than FIFO because older, cheaper costs are matched against sales
Profit under FIFO and LIFO will always be equal regardless of price movements
FIFO gives a higher profit than LIFO because cost of goods sold under FIFO is based on older, lower costs
questions.e: Under FIFO, the cost of goods sold is based on the oldest (cheaper) stock, so cost of sales is lower and profit is higher during rising prices. LIFO matches the newest (more expensive) stock against sales, giving a higher cost of sales and lower profit.
questions.p: Under FIFO, cost of goods sold dey use the old cheap stock, so cost of sales go small and profit go high when price dey rise. LIFO dey use the new expensive stock, so cost of sales go high and profit go small.

questions.q: A wholesaler's stock card for bags of rice shows: Opening stock 40 bags at ₦100 each, Purchase 1 of 60 bags at ₦110 each, Purchase 2 of 100 bags at ₦120 each. During the period, 150 bags were sold. Using the periodic weighted average method, what is the cost of goods sold?
questions.e: Total cost = (40x100)+(60x110)+(100x120) = 4,000+6,600+12,000 = ₦22,600 for 200 bags, giving an average cost of ₦113 per bag. Cost of goods sold = 150 x ₦113 = ₦16,950.
questions.p: Total cost = (40x100)+(60x110)+(100x120) = 4,000+6,600+12,000 = ₦22,600 for 200 bags, so average cost na ₦113 per bag. Cost of goods sold = 150 x ₦113 = ₦16,950.

questions.q: A supermarket's stock record for cooking oil in May shows: Opening stock 80 units at ₦25 each, and a purchase on 12th May of 120 units at ₦30 each. On 25th May, 150 units were sold. What is the difference between the closing stock value under FIFO and under LIFO?
questions.e: Closing stock units = 80+120-150 = 50. Under FIFO, the 50 remaining units come from the 12th May purchase at ₦30, giving 50x30 = ₦1,500. Under LIFO, the 50 remaining units come from the opening stock at ₦25, giving 50x25 = ₦1,250. Difference = ₦1,500 - ₦1,250 = ₦250.
questions.p: Wetin remain na 50 units (80+120-150). Under FIFO, the 50 units na from the May 12 purchase at ₦30, so 50x30 = ₦1,500. Under LIFO, the 50 units na from opening stock at ₦25, so 50x25 = ₦1,250. Difference = ₦1,500 minus ₦1,250 = ₦250.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's shop has current assets of ₦240,000 and current liabilities of ₦120,000. What is the current ratio?
questions.e: Current ratio = Current assets ÷ Current liabilities = 240,000 ÷ 120,000 = 2, written as 2:1. This shows the business has ₦2 of current assets for every ₦1 of current liabilities.
questions.p: Current ratio na Current assets divide by Current liabilities = 240,000 ÷ 120,000 = 2, so e be 2:1. Na so dem dey write am.

questions.q: Which formula correctly represents the acid test (quick) ratio?
questions.e: The acid test ratio removes stock from current assets because stock is not quickly convertible to cash. It then divides the remainder by current liabilities to test immediate liquidity.
questions.p: Acid test ratio dey remove stock from current assets because stock no dey quick turn to cash. Na the remaining one dem divide by current liabilities to check if business fit pay quick debts.

questions.q: Chidinma Stores recorded sales of ₦500,000 and cost of goods sold of ₦350,000 for the year. What is the gross profit margin?
questions.e: Gross profit = 500,000 - 350,000 = 150,000. Gross profit margin = (150,000 ÷ 500,000) x 100 = 30%. This shows gross profit as a percentage of sales.
questions.p: Gross profit = 500,000 - 350,000 = 150,000. Gross profit margin = (150,000 ÷ 500,000) x 100 = 30%. Na so dem take find am.

questions.q: Emeka Ventures had sales of ₦800,000 and net profit of ₦96,000 for the year ended 31 December. Calculate the net profit margin.
questions.e: Net profit margin = (Net profit ÷ Sales) x 100 = (96,000 ÷ 800,000) x 100 = 12%. This tells us how much profit is made from every ₦100 of sales.
questions.p: Net profit margin = (Net profit ÷ Sales) x 100 = (96,000 ÷ 800,000) x 100 = 12%. Na how much profit dem get for every ₦100 sales be that.

questions.q: A trader's opening stock was ₦40,000, closing stock ₦60,000, and cost of goods sold for the year was ₦500,000. What is the rate of stock turnover?
questions.e: Average stock = (40,000 + 60,000) ÷ 2 = 50,000. Stock turnover = Cost of goods sold ÷ Average stock = 500,000 ÷ 50,000 = 10 times a year.
questions.p: Average stock = (40,000 + 60,000) ÷ 2 = 50,000. Stock turnover = 500,000 ÷ 50,000 = 10 times for the year.

questions.q: Funke Enterprises made credit sales of ₦720,000 during the year. Trade debtors at year end stood at ₦90,000. Using 360 days in a year, calculate the average debtors' collection period.
questions.e: Collection period = (Debtors ÷ Credit sales) x 360 days = (90,000 ÷ 720,000) x 360 = 45 days. This shows on average how long it takes debtors to pay what they owe.
questions.p: Collection period = (Debtors ÷ Credit sales) x 360 = (90,000 ÷ 720,000) x 360 = 45 days. Na the average time wey debtors dey take pay their debt.

questions.q: A company's net profit before interest and tax is ₦150,000, while its capital employed (total assets minus current liabilities) is ₦1,000,000. What is the return on capital employed (ROCE)?
questions.e: ROCE = (Net profit before interest and tax ÷ Capital employed) x 100 = (150,000 ÷ 1,000,000) x 100 = 15%. ROCE measures how efficiently a business uses its capital to generate profit.
questions.p: ROCE = (Net profit before interest and tax ÷ Capital employed) x 100 = (150,000 ÷ 1,000,000) x 100 = 15%. Na how well the business dey use the capital wey dem get to make profit.

questions.q: A business has a long-term bank loan of ₦400,000 and equity capital (ordinary shares plus reserves) of ₦600,000. What is the gearing ratio, calculated as long-term loan divided by total of loan and equity?
questions.e: Gearing ratio = Long-term loan ÷ (Loan + Equity) x 100 = 400,000 ÷ (400,000 + 600,000) x 100 = 40%. This shows that 40% of the business's long-term finance comes from borrowed funds.
questions.p: Gearing ratio = Long-term loan ÷ (Loan + Equity) x 100 = 400,000 ÷ 1,000,000 x 100 = 40%. E mean say 40% of the long-term money wey business get na loan.
